title: Capital Gains on Compulsory Acquisition of Industrial Asset: Section 45(5) & Section 54D
subject: DT
provision_raw:
Section 45(5) & Section 54D: Capital Gains on Compulsory Acquisition of Industrial Asset
Statutory Provision	Eligibility Criteria / Pre-condition	Statutory Window	Exemption / Tax Treatment
Section 45(5)	Compulsory acquisition of capital asset under any statutory law	Year of initial receipt	Chargeable to tax in the Financial Year in which compensation is first received
Section 54D	Land or building used for industrial undertaking for ≥ 2 years prior to transfer	3 years after transfer date	Exempt to the extent of cost of new industrial land or building
story_summary: Mr. Rajesh's chemical factory land in Palakkad is compulsorily acquired by the government for highway expansion. After receiving the compensation, he learns that under Section 45(5), tax is payable only in the year of actual receipt, and he can claim Section 54D exemption by reinvesting in a new industrial plot within 3 years.

slides.scene_purpose: Setup: Government acquires Rajesh's industrial factory land and pays initial compensation.
slides.dialogue_manglish: Namukku aadyam Mr. Rajesh-inte case nokkaam. Palakkad-il 'Rajesh Chemicals' enna industrial factory running aayirunnu. 2023-il National Highway expansion-u vendi Government eyaalude industrial land compulsorily acquire cheythu ₹100 Lakhs compensation nalki.

slots.title: Compulsory Acquisition of Industrial Land
slots.note: Compulsory acquisition under statutory law triggers capital gains rules under Sec 45(5).

slides.scene_purpose: Checking basic pre-conditions for Section 54D exemption eligibility.
slides.dialogue_manglish: Section 54D exemption claim cheyyaan multi-criteria conditions pass aaganamanu. Aadyathethu, transfer compulsory acquisition aayirikkanam. Randaamatheedhu, aa land/building minimum 2 years industrial undertaking-nu vendi use cheythirikkanam. Rajesh 3 years use cheythathukondu gate open aayi!

slots.title: Section 54D Pre-Condition Checklist

conditions.text: Transfer is by way of Compulsory Acquisition under statutory law
Asset used for Industrial Undertaking for >= 2 years prior to transfer

slots.note: Both conditions must be satisfied to qualify for Section 54D roll-over relief.

slides.scene_purpose: Highlighting the special timing rule for compulsory acquisition taxability.
slides.dialogue_manglish: Ivide oru important tax point undu! Section 45(5) prakaram capital gain taxable aagunnadhu acquisition order vanna year-il alla, initial compensation actual aayi receive cheyyunna Financial Year-ilaanu.

slots.title: Statutory Timing Rule - Section 45(5)
slots.statement: Capital Gains on Compulsory Acquisition are chargeable to tax in the Financial Year in which initial compensation is FIRST RECEIVED.
slots.support_line: Not in the year of acquisition order or transfer date.

slides.scene_purpose: Timeline check for purchasing or constructing new industrial land/building.
slides.dialogue_manglish: Section 54D exemption kinna 3-year statutory window undu. Acquisition transfer date muthal 3 years-nu ullil puthiya industrial land or building purchase cheyyuka-yo construct cheyyuka-yo venam. Rajesh 1.5 years-il puthiya plot vangiyathinaal timing perfectly inside the window!

slots.title: Statutory Window for Reinvestment
slots.note: Reinvestment must occur within 3 years after the date of transfer.

slides.scene_purpose: Computing final capital gain after deducting Section 54D exemption.
slides.dialogue_manglish: Inni final tax calculation nokkaam. Rajesh-nte Total Capital Gain ₹60 Lakhs aayirunnu. Eeyal puthiya industrial land-il ₹50 Lakhs reinvest cheythathinaal, Sec 54D prakaram full ₹50 Lakhs exempt aagum. Remainder ₹10 Lakhs maathramaanu taxable LTCG!

slots.title: Computation of Taxable Capital Gain

chunks.label: Exemption u/s 54D (Cost of New Industrial Asset)

slots.note: Exemption is limited to the lower of Capital Gain or Cost of New Asset.
